lines.en: What fascinates scientists about Mars is the evidence that rivers once flowed across its surface.
It is believed that the universe contains more stars than there are grains of sand on all our beaches.
Not until the telescope was invented did we understand that Earth is not the center of everything.
However far a spacecraft may travel, it still carries a little piece of human curiosity with it.
Were we to find even the simplest form of life on another planet, it would change how we see ourselves forever.
The astronaut is said to have cried when she saw the Earth from space for the first time.
It is not the distance that makes space travel difficult, but the cost of leaving Earth's gravity.
Little did the ancient astronomers know that the strange lights they watched were entire galaxies.
What a night in the desert teaches you is that the sky is not a ceiling, but a window.
Rarely do we look up and realize that the light reaching our eyes left its star years ago.
What keeps scientists searching is the question of whether we are truly alone in the universe.
It is the moon, not the sun, that controls the tides that shape our coastlines.
So vast is the universe that even the nearest star system lies beyond a lifetime of travel.
Were an asteroid to approach Earth, the world's space agencies would finally have to work as one team.
It was only after the first moon landing that people understood how small and fragile our planet is.
